To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) cells with a small front (i.e., narrow pseudopod), which is a common characteristic of amoeboid cells, cannot move collectively; and (b) cells with a large, broad front, which is a common trait of mesenchymal cells, exhibit coherent migration without explicit alignment.

(i) the model cell exhibits contact inhibition of locomtion (CIL), which is a hallmark of cell migration, (ii) CIL can induce coherent migration of cells, (iii) the shape of the cell front (e.g., the width of a pseudopod) can determine the collective motion of cells, and (iv) density waves can propagate against the direction in which cells move, which is similar to the behaviour observed in biological experiments.

(1) the collective migration of cells crawling on an adhesive substrate is highly non-tri- vial and depends on both cell shape and contact-inhibition of locomotion; and (2) cells with a large pseudopod (e.g., lamellipodium), which is common in many types of migrating cells, exhibit coherent migration without explicit alignment mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cell shape on collective motion of cells crawling.
a minimal model of crawling cells and the collective motion of such cells.
the collective motion of cells crawling under CIL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model cells exhibit a rich variety of collective behaviour depending on the shape of the cell and whether CIL occurs.
contact inhibition of locomotions plays a crucial role to facilitate collective cell migration, which is consistent with experimental observations.
the collective motion of cells is determined by both the cell shape and CIL, which are the two fundamental characteristics of cell motility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CIL is essential to the formation of coherent motion in a dense cell population.
the model reproduces the essential features of collective migration, such as cell sorting, collective motion, and the formation of waves and clusters.
contact inhibition is not always a hindrance to cell migration, and the shape of the cell is a critical factor that determines how cells respond to contact inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CIL is not a prerequisite for collective migration, which is contrary to a common belief in the field.
the collective motion of cells crawling in a 2-dimensional space can be described by a simple model with only two parameters, which can be easily extended to a 3-dimensional space.
the shape of the cell is an important factor in the emergence of collective motion.
